Lumentum remains confident in an ultra-high-power laser chip demand ramp in the second half of calendar 2027, ahead of customer scale-up deployments in calendar 2028. Because the first phase of scale-up optical connections spans across compute racks within a cluster, the ramp applies to any topology larger than one rack. Ultra-high-power laser revenue is expected to reach roughly the $50 million mark by the end of calendar 2026, with the first triple-digit ($100M+) quarter expected in fiscal Q3 FY2027.

quarterly_data.signal: NPO (near-packaged optics) called 'completely additive' and 'significantly increasing the optical TAM.' Two laser types are being evaluated for NPO: a mid-power laser integrated directly into the optical engine, and a high-power laser in an external light source module. Lumentum's NPO/CPO laser family spans 120 mW, 150 mW, and 400 mW output levels off common design and process know-how. Wupen Yuen: each NPO set carries ~6.4T of bandwidth, roughly four times a local module, and NPO should hit the market in the late 2027 / 2028 timeframe to enable optical scale-up.

The margin gap between CW and EML 'has closed considerably' since the prior call (EML still better). Better-than-expected output in Japan is being allocated to CW, and Lumentum is now shipping CW lasers in a relatively meaningful way into the 200G-per-lane silicon photonics opportunity, on top of internal deployment in its own transceivers.

products.product: probe cards for HBM/DRAM wafer test
CPO / silicon-photonics wafer test - insertion-1 known-good-die probe on PIC wafers, plus engineering probers

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM probe cards hit another RECORD on an HBM demand step-up, with another record guided for Q2 — most of the incremental growth from a SECOND customer adopting FormFactor's differentiated Smart Matrix full-wafer contactor (tests hundreds of completed HBM stacks simultaneously at the 10Gbps+ I/O rates of HBM4). Smart Matrix is critical for stacked-die test insertions that give the final test of the HBM stack before it is combined with GPUs/custom ASICs in advanced packaging like TSMC CoWoS. Share gains expected to continue as pin/IO speeds and stack bandwidth rise relentlessly from HBM3 -> HBM4 -> HBM5. End market: DRAM remains SUPPLY-CONSTRAINED overall; customers dynamically shifting wafer-start mix between HBM and DDR designs (probe cards are chip-design-specific, so FormFactor mix shifts with them).
quarterly_data.figure: Record DRAM probe cards; 2nd Smart Matrix HBM customer; HBM4 10Gbps+ test; DRAM supply-constrained

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: HBM IS NOW ~TWO-THIRDS OF FORMFACTOR'S DRAM REVENUE, on 'two customers' continued adoption' of the differentiated SmartMatrix FULL-WAFER CONTACTOR in high-speed HBM4 - it tests HUNDREDS OF COMPLETED HBM STACKS SIMULTANEOUSLY at HBM4's 10 GIGABIT-PLUS PER-PIN I/O rate. Why it matters structurally: this stacked-die test insertion is what 'ensures a KNOWN GOOD HBM STACK before it's combined with costly GPUs or custom ASICs' inside advanced packaging flows - TSMC's CoWoS and Intel's EMIB are both named. Competitive split made explicit: FormFactor's strong share is at the high-speed FINAL stack test at two of the three HBM makers, while 'lots of competition' sits in the core-die insertions that resemble ordinary DRAM wafer sort; the company is partnering with all three makers as speeds and stack heights rise from HBM4 to 4E to HBM5.

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY / THE DDR SNAP-BACK, SEEN FROM THE PROBE-CARD SIDE: Q3 DRAM revenue is guided COMPARABLE to the record Q2 'but with a significant underlying SHIFT FROM HBM TO DDR'. The reason is the memory shortage itself - 'as you've heard recently from all our major DRAM customers, the supply environment continues to be EXTREMELY CONSTRAINED, and our customers are shifting their WAFER START MIX TO DDR DESIGNS to capture the profit opportunity provided by significant DDR PRICE INCREASES'. Because probe cards are specific to each customer chip design, FormFactor's mix tracks those wafer-start shifts one-for-one - making its DRAM mix a near-real-time proxy for where DRAM makers are actually pointing capacity 'while these unusual end market conditions persist'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 DRAM flat QoQ but mix shifts HBM -> DDR as makers chase DDR pricing

quarterly_data.signal: CO-PACKAGED OPTICS TEST IS RUNNING AHEAD OF PLAN. FormFactor entered 2026 guiding $10-20M of CPO revenue, raised it to the high end a quarter ago, and now expects to EXCEED $20M BY THE END OF Q3 and to 'significantly exceed the $20 million level for the year overall'; systems-segment revenue nearly DOUBLED sequentially to a record $48.5M largely on this acceleration. Two drivers: growing CPO chip volumes planned for later this year, and leadership in 'the all-important TEST INSERTION ONE, which ensures KNOWN GOOD DIE on the PHOTONIC INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (PIC) wafer before it's combined with the electrical integrated circuit (EIC) to form the optical module in SCALE-UP AND SCALE-OUT network switches'. Management frames this as 'the very early stages of widespread adoption of silicon photonics in the broader semiconductor industry' as 'traditional copper interconnect is reaching physical limits in speed, heat and energy consumption', backed by a decade-long lab-to-fab first-mover advantage; served market sized at ~$400M by 2030. CPO revenue is recognized through the leading foundry (a 10% customer at 11% of Q2 revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CPO revenue to significantly exceed $20M (>$20M by end-Q3); ~$400M served market by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: AI test intensity is compounding because design margins are shrinking: higher data rates, lower latency and the requirement that AI fabrics be LOSSLESS mean customers 'can no longer guarantee anything by design' and must test in production too. A compute or switch tray has gone from tens to HUNDREDS of IC pinouts - more insertion points - tested at signal level (VNAs, oscilloscopes), at bit level (new portfolio) and at protocol/packet level (AI workload emulators). The move from monolithic chips to CHIPLET architectures adds interoperability emulation, and customers now ask for emulation environments that stress a chip while it exercises a model (thermal shutdown, all cores active at higher power and speed). The ecosystem is shifting from a homogeneous integrated vertical stack to a HETEROGENEOUS one - GPU/CPU/DPU mixes and a growing number of protocols at every layer of the stack - which broadens Keysight's addressable tail. The four wireline pillars (AI infrastructure scaling, speed transitions, silicon photonics, system-level emulation) all drove growth. Hyperscaler engagement (rooted in the Ixia acquisition ~5 years ago) is deepening as they integrate Keysight pre-silicon emulation and workload solutions into their development pipelines; hyperscalers plus the model companies are ~10% OF REVENUE DIRECTLY but drive large downstream influence, and many are building their own in-house silicon. Switch designers use Keysight emulators to validate network performance across AI workloads and protocols; interconnect manufacturers use high-fidelity analyzers to characterize high-speed backplanes for signal integrity and manufacturing yield.
quarterly_data.figure: Hundreds of IC pinouts per tray; hyperscalers ~10% of revenue direct; chiplet + workload emulation

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor was a RECORD quarter within a record Electronic Industrial Solutions Group (EISG revenue $501M, +21%, with double-digit order growth across all three markets), driven by ongoing CAPACITY EXPANSION FOR ADVANCED NODES, high-bandwidth memory and silicon photonics. Given increasing adoption of optical interconnects, COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION OF SILICON PHOTONICS IS ACCELERATING ACROSS LEADING FOUNDRIES AND IDMs. Demand for semiconductor R&D solutions was also healthy, and engagement with industry leaders gives good visibility into their requirements into next year and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: EISG semi a RECORD; wafer-test capacity expanding across advanced nodes + memory + SiPh

quarterly_data.signal: Company-wide, SUPPLY rather than demand is the limiter: orders $2.091B (+56%, second straight quarter above $2B) against revenue $1.846B (+36%), book-to-bill above 1.1 for two consecutive quarters and backlog built in the quarter. The supply environment is 'less flexible today than a year ago'; the binding constraint has moved from internal channel capacity to INCOMING PARTS, with numerous players competing for the same component suppliers. Management expects supply to be 'nonlinear' and 'a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters'. Mitigations carry a lag: an 18-month+ supply-chain planning horizon, redesigning some products at the margin to accommodate SECOND SOURCES, and longer-term supply agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: Orders $2.091B vs rev $1.846B; B2B >1.1 two quarters; incoming parts the constraint

Product positioning: special etchants for sub-2nm GAA, next-generation CMP slurry and precursors for HBM4 stacking; ultra-high-purity chemicals supplied at near-exclusive levels to Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix from the leading-edge ramp and ultra-high-layer V-NAND development stage; a completed portfolio of TSV formation and planarisation materials for HBM4 and chiplet structures to lift high-value-added revenue; display unit expanding into glass-substrate processing materials for next-generation packaging; customers' processes moving to GAA and to HBM / 400+ layer NAND, with joint development from the process-design stage. US entities Soulbrain TX LLC (2022) and Soulbrain RASA TX LLC (2024) respond in real time to customers' new fab lines in Texas and North America; the Xi'an entity supports China memory lines. Semiconductor material ASPs +5% vs FY2025 while raw-material costs rose +14%; semiconductor materials 85% of H1 revenue, +31% company-wide revenue growth.

quarterly_data.signal: NAND/DRAM scarcity is the defining constraint. CEO Wallace Kou: the AI super cycle has driven substantial HBM, DRAM, NAND and HDD price increases and 'mounting substrate and supply pressure,' and he expects the scarcity to persist 'likely until 2028 when new fabs come online.' DRAM and NAND now account for almost 56% of total BOM cost on a low-end smartphone, forcing OEMs to trim specifications; smartphone units are still expected down 10-15% in 2026. NAND makers are redirecting focus and CapEx to DRAM and HBM, deemphasising eMMC/UFS and exiting automotive - which hands share to Silicon Motion's module-maker customers and gives it stronger pricing power. Long-standing relationships let Silicon Motion secure NAND from multiple suppliers through the shortage, which management calls a significant and enduring differentiator.

quarterly_data.signal: Ferri for Automotive and Enterprise Boot Drive solutions MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially and now represent nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago. These are controller-plus-NAND solutions, so ASPs are much higher than controller-only (and higher than MonTitan). The DRAM-less boot drive is the crown jewel: conventional DRAM-based boot drives for server CPUs stay with the NAND makers, but DPUs, TPUs, NPUs and switches favour DRAM-less designs for cost, security and performance - and NAND makers have no DRAM-less PCIe SSD controllers and little incentive to build them for a market where densities are only 256GB-512GB. A server rack can carry more than 30 or 40 boot drives, and per-drive capacity should rise. Management sees little competition from either NAND makers or module makers, and said Ferri plus Boot Drive reaching roughly one third of revenue in 2027 is 'certainly a possibility' given current backlog and pipeline.

quarterly_data.signal: On NAND supply: 'we still able to get supply, but unfortunately supply not enough to what we need... We have supply, but supply still not enough what we need.' Demand is too strong, so price will keep rising but at a decelerating rate toward saturation, at which point suppliers start choosing whom to ship. quarterly_data.signal: THE CORE THESIS, sharpened: 'While COMPUTE CYCLES CAN BE REUSED, DATA COMPOUNDS.' Training creates the initial data foundation, inference generates data continuously, agentic systems multiply the volume and frequency, and physical AI accelerates the cycle further - so storage demand shifts from a one-time infrastructure build to the ongoing compounding of retained data. The largest AI platforms now process TENS OF BILLIONS OF TOKENS PER MINUTE and BILLIONS OF PROMPTS PER DAY with token volumes growing severalfold YoY. Roughly 80% OF DATA STORED IN A HYPERSCALE DATA CENTER SITS ON HARD DISK DRIVES, and management expects that to hold. For PHYSICAL AI (autonomous vehicles, robotics, humanoids, industrial automation) real-world data is INSUFFICIENT to train the models, so operators generate and must store SYNTHETIC DATA SETS for reinforcement learning - a new demand vector. On inference specifically: storing generated context is MORE ECONOMICAL THAN RE-RUNNING IT through compute and memory. Core cloud services (notably stored video/collaboration recordings) remain an underappreciated parallel driver, and cheaper open-source Asian models are viewed as demand-positive since more model access means more data

quarterly_data.signal: CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
quarterly_data.figure: Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

The growth has two compounding drivers: the shift to optical networking itself, and the fact that what could previously be done in CMOS at 50-gig and 100-gig per lane cannot be done at 200-gig and definitely not at 400-gig per lane, forcing transimpedance amplifiers and increasingly the drivers out into high-performance analog processes like SiGe. High-performance analog also appears in near and co-packaged optics depending on architecture. GF is expanding SiGe capacity at Burlington, Vermont and qualifying 300-millimeter SiGe in Singapore for additional capacity, better economics and higher fT/fMAX performance. quarterly_data.signal: IP, software and custom silicon: GF completed the acquisition of the Synopsys ARC processor IP Solutions business in June, adding CPU, DSP, NPU and RISC-V technologies, a software development toolkit and application-specific processor design capability - over 150 patents, 300 existing customers and 400 R&D engineers. Combined with MIPS, this lets GF engage customers earlier in the design cycle for edge AI and on-device inference in automotive, industrial and robotics. Full-year 2026 technology services contribution from MIPS plus ARC was RAISED to $100-120 million from a prior $60-100 million, skewed roughly one third Q3 and two thirds Q4, and technology services revenue is now expected toward the high end of the 10-12% of total revenue range with gross margin significantly above corporate targets. Design wins in the quarter included 3 strategic chiplet wins with Lockheed Martin on FinFET and FDX, an expanded FinFET win with Microchip, a first-ever PMIC design win with MediaTek on the BCD platform, an ADAS radar tape-out for Bosch on FDX, and a new microLED display backplane win for augmented reality wearables at a leading hyperscaler.
quarterly_data.figure: Technology services contribution raised to $100M-$120M for 2026 (from $60M-$100M); ARC adds 150 patents, 300 customers, 400 R&D engineers

quarterly_data.signal: End-market split and the memory-shortage read-across: smart mobile devices were ~36% of Q2 revenue, up 15% sequentially but down 6% year over year, and are now expected to DECLINE BY A LOW-TEENS PERCENTAGE in 2026 because 2026 handset forecasts have been cut meaningfully on continued memory pricing and associated shortages. Automotive was ~19% of revenue, down 13% sequentially and 10% year over year on customer-led shipment timing, but full-year low-double-digit growth is still expected weighted to Q4. Home and industrial IoT was ~19% of revenue, up 30% sequentially and 10% year over year - its fastest year-over-year growth since 2022 - and the full-year outlook was raised to 10-15% growth from mid-single digits, partly because mobile customers reallocated demand into IoT connectivity applications. GF credited a deliberately flexible manufacturing footprint for reusing capacity to capture data-center upside as mobile weakened.
quarterly_data.figure: Smart mobile ~36% of revenue, FY2026 down low teens on memory shortage; automotive ~19%; IoT ~19%, FY2026 raised to 10-15% growth

quarterly_data.signal: Cash and capital returns: Q2 cash flow from operations was $405 million and capex net of government grant proceeds was $408 million (roughly 23% of revenue), leaving adjusted free cash flow at negative $3 million as previously guided. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $3.3 billion against $1.1 billion of total debt, with a $1 billion revolving credit facility undrawn. GF paid its first-ever quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share on July 14 and declared another $0.12 per share payable October 9, 2026. Approximately $100 million remains under the share repurchase authorization; the stated objective is to return up to 50% of trailing-twelve-month non-IFRS adjusted free cash flow after investments over time.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 OCF $405M; capex $408M (~23% of revenue); adjusted FCF -$3M; $3.3B cash and securities; first-ever dividend $0.12/share

quarterly_data.signal: Announced a multibillion-dollar strategic partnership with Renesas expanding access to GF technologies (FDX, BCD, feature-rich CMOS with integrated non-volatile memory) for SoCs, power devices and MCUs targeting data-center power, ADAS and secure industrial IoT; tape-outs already underway and expected to meaningfully contribute to GF's data-center business ramp. Continues GaN-on-silicon foundry (8-inch US pivot) for power.
quarterly_data.figure: Renesas multibillion-$ partnership (FDX/BCD power); GaN-on-Si 8-inch US

quarterly_data.signal: Data center power is GF's third named growth pillar alongside silicon photonics and SiGe. In July GF closed a strategic acquihire of the custom power team from Photon Technologies in Europe, bringing an experienced design team focused on INTEGRATED VOLTAGE REGULATORS (IVRs). Combined with GF's BCD, GaN and integrated-inductor capabilities, the goal is a new power architecture that brings power conversion closer to the processor to meet the efficiency, power density, bandwidth, high-current and transient-response requirements of next-generation XPUs. CEO Tim Breen framed it directly: 'IVR is to power what CPO is to photonics' - moving from traditional industrial/automotive-style power modules to a much more wafer-level integrated solution delivering power closer to the chip. The Photon team is already engaged with a number of existing GF customers, and early feedback from fabless companies, IDMs and hyperscalers has been very positive.

quarterly_data.signal: GF closed a first-of-a-kind design win for SMART POWER STAGE GATE DRIVERS on its BCD platform for data center power applications, which management called one notable step into a rapidly evolving market. The quarter also brought a significant automotive power design win for 5-volt and 10-volt power management integrated circuits on BCD, and a first-ever PMIC design win with long-standing customer MediaTek on the same platform - evidence that the BCD power platform is expanding across data center, automotive and mobile.
quarterly_data.figure: First-of-a-kind smart power stage gate driver design win on BCD; automotive 5V/10V PMIC win; first-ever MediaTek PMIC win

products.product: ZeroFlap AECs, optical DSPs (Robin/Cardinal), SiPho PICs (Dust Photonics), retimers for AI clusters

AECs are the core engine: ZeroFlap active electrical cables deliver 'up to 1,000x greater reliability than commodity laser-based optical modules' at much lower power — now the preferred in-rack solution and used multi-rack up to 7 meters; strong hyperscaler + NeoCloud adoption at 100G/lane with 200G/lane emerging; PCIe Gen 6 AEC family on track. Thesis: AI infrastructure is 'increasingly constrained not by compute but by the reliability and efficiency of the connectivity fabric'.

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 = optical INFLECTION: optical DSPs (Robin 100G/lane, Cardinal 200G/lane), SiPho PICs and ZeroFlap optics expected to EACH exceed $100M — total optical revenue >$600M in FY27, ramp accelerating in H2. Dust Photonics acquisition (closed late May 2026) adds differentiated silicon-photonics PIC technology spanning 800G/1.6T with a roadmap to 3.2T+ — its architecture needs SUBSTANTIALLY FEWER LASERS, easing industry supply constraints, and provides a direct path to CPO/NPO with initial revenue expected FY2028. Also: 200G/lane retimers supporting Ethernet + UALINK + eSUN; micro-LED active cables (AEC reliability at 30m optical reach) and OmniConnect 'Weaver' memory-IO gearbox both ramping FY2028.
quarterly_data.figure: FY27 optical >$600M total; Dust SiPho cuts laser count; CPO/NPO revenue FY28

Non-GAAP gross margin 68% (midpoint of guide); non-GAAP operating expenses $95.2 million (+16% sequentially, above guide on strong R&D investment); non-GAAP operating income $230.6 million (operating margin 48.2%); non-GAAP net income a record $236.3 million (up 140% year-over-year per the CEO / more than doubled; +4% sequential vs $226.7 million in Q4), non-GAAP net margin 49.3%. quarterly_data.signal: AECs remain Credo's largest business and continue to grow: DEEP RELATIONSHIPS WITH FIVE HYPERSCALERS and expanding NeoCloud engagement; AEC penetration increasing within existing customers as deployments scale, with the transition to 200G per lane / 1.6T ports ahead as the next growth vector. At 800G, copper AECs replaced laser-based optical transceivers for the GPU-to-first-switch connection on reliability and, secondarily, lower power. Management frames AECs as the 1m-7m segment of the pluggable transceiver market — with optical transceivers alone forecast to grow from 60 million units in 2026 to 175 million units by 2030 — and 1.6T AECs will deliver up to 6.5m reach, with some contribution in second-half fiscal 2027 and a much bigger ramp in fiscal 2028. AEC revenue more than doubled from 2024-2025 and more than tripled from 2025-2026; AECs keep growing, though slower than optics, which grows from a smaller base into a larger market.
quarterly_data.figure: Five hyperscaler AEC relationships; 1.6T AECs up to 6.5m reach — H2 FY2027 contribution, much bigger in fiscal 2028; transceiver market 60M to 175M units by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Optical is the fastest-growing business, firmly on track for MORE THAN $600 million of FY2027 optical revenue. Optical DSPs: record Q1 revenue across 50G and 100G per lane deployments with a long tail for 800G ports; at 200G per lane, customer engagement with the 1.6T DSP is strong across both fully retimed and LRO solutions, and FIRST 1.6T DSP REVENUE remains on track for later this fiscal year. Silicon photonics: FIRST SiPho PIC revenue recognized in Q1 following the DustPhotonics acquisition, with initial wins in 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers expected to ramp throughout the year; the Dust team has secured DESIGN WINS WITH TWO MAJOR PLAYERS for next-generation ramps in FY2028 (possibly starting late this fiscal year) — the first two wins do NOT include the Credo DSP, leaving co-marketing upside. ZeroFlap Optics: production shipments underway, with additional customer ramps during fiscal 2027 across both 800G and 1.6T at both hyperscalers and neoclouds; the PILOT software platform provides continuous telemetry (real-time eye height, SNR, post-FEC histograms on all six links between XPU and switch, plus ESD-damage and fiber-dust detection) targeting cluster bring-up in five or six days versus six to eight weeks and driving to 99% uptime or higher — customers have cited link flaps costing greater than 10% or even approaching 20% of GPU utilization.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 optical >$600M; first 1.6T DSP revenue later this fiscal year; first SiPho PIC revenue in Q1; two major PIC design wins for FY2028 ramps

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up optics push: Credo joined the Open Compute Project MSA consortium (open CPX) and sees increasing customer activity around NPO for scale-up networks, with CONFIRMED DESIGN WINS expected to begin ramping in fiscal 2028. Scale-up requires roughly 10x more density than scale-out pluggables — the industry conversation spans XPO, CPX, NPO and ultimately CPO — and Credo is approaching it agnostically: leading with the silicon photonics PIC in all NPO solutions including CPX, pursuing component sales where customers prefer them and complete optical engines / system-level solutions long term, bringing pluggable-ecosystem advantages (telemetry, interoperability, serviceability) to the consortium.
quarterly_data.figure: NPO scale-up design wins confirmed, ramping fiscal 2028; 10x density improvement needed vs scale-out

quarterly_data.signal: Retimers delivered record Q1 revenue, driven primarily by scale-up deployments of the Screaming Eagle retimer at 100G per lane, with the Blue Heron retimer beginning to contribute at 200G per lane; the Toucan retimer opportunity grows as PCIe Gen 6 adoption increases, and Screaming Eagle/Blue Heron span both Ethernet and UALink. Emerging growth engines with revenue beginning fiscal 2028: (1) Active LED Cables (ALCs) using microLED emitters — AEC-class reliability and power with reach of up to 30m; demonstrations planned at OFC in October; framed as a multi-billion-dollar pluggable-transceiver opportunity with a scale-up follow-on. (2) OmniConnect — a licensed low-power short-reach SerDes (reach up to 10in) plus Weaver gearboxes (LPDDR5 first, then LPDDR6, no XPU re-tape-out needed for the memory transition) attacking the memory fan-out limits of inference; potentially THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS of Credo content per GPU; first customer Positron's first announced product scales memory capacity up to 2TB (fitting frontier models fully in memory), and the roadmap targets bandwidth comparable to HBM5.
quarterly_data.figure: Record retimer revenue; ALCs up to 30m with OFC demos in October; OmniConnect thousands of dollars of content per GPU, revenue from fiscal 2028; Positron product up to 2TB memory

quarterly_data.figure: ~200k units/mo now -> >650k/mo end-2026 -> >930k/mo end-2027 (>50% from Texas); TX footprint >1.6M sqft; booked through Q2 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CPO / ELSFP EXTERNAL LASER SOURCE ECONOMICS: ELSFP (external light source for co-packaged optics) is in very limited production now, ramping later in 2026 and through 2027 to ~400,000 PIECES PER MONTH IN 2028. Laser power scaling is the constraint: CPO/ELSFP uses a 300mW laser vs 70mW in an 800G transceiver and 100mW in a 1.6T transceiver, with die size ~6x larger, so meeting CPO demand requires the industry laser market to be 8-10x BIGGER than today; the next generation of ELSFP moves to DWDM, where yield loss is 40-50% worse than 1310nm. Laser capacity carries a 21-24 MONTH equipment-to-high-volume lead time. AOI is engaged with ~5 CPO customers on 3-4 year demand; several have already qualified AOI on fixed-wavelength CPO laser / ELSFP, with DWDM the current focus. High-volume ELSFP manufacturing is 'more like late Q3 next year' (late 2027). Houston laser fab capacity to grow ~300% by Q3 2027 plus a SECOND FAB cleanroom ~4x the size of the current facility (adding MOCVD, epi, steppers). Margin mix: laser gross margin 55-65%, ELSFP module ('EOSAP') >50%, both landing H2 2027. AOI is absent from first-generation CPO deployments purely because laser capacity must first feed AOI's own transceivers.
quarterly_data.figure: ELSFP ~400k pcs/month in 2028; 300mW CPO laser vs 70mW(800G)/100mW(1.6T); industry laser capacity needs 8-10x; laser GM 55-65%

quarterly_data.signal: BOTTLENECK HAS MOVED FROM LASERS TO DSP/TIA: because AOI makes its own lasers in-house it avoids the laser shortage that management calls 'the biggest bottleneck right now for the transceiver business' and 'the number one issue' for competitors; AOI's binding constraints for 800G/1.6T are instead DSP and TIA supply, where 'the whole supply chain is very tight' for 1.6T - AOI says its supplier ranks it FOURTH priority under a long-term partnership, with calls once or twice a week. INDIUM PHOSPHIDE SUBSTRATE: supply secured into end-2027 and 'incrementally better' than last quarter - not currently a limiter; AOI has just moved to 4-INCH substrate volume manufacturing and buys from 2 European + 2 Japanese + 3 Chinese suppliers, and is negotiating partnerships or a possible JOINT VENTURE with 2-3 of them for 2028-2029 volumes (laser capacity growing 'much more than a factor of 10'). Proprietary in-house production machinery insulates AOI from the industry's equipment-delivery bottlenecks.
quarterly_data.figure: DSP/TIA = binding constraint (AOI ranked 4th priority); InP substrate secured to end-2027; 4-inch substrate volume production

quarterly_data.signal: NPO and XPO positioning: MACOM has BETWEEN 10 AND 20 ACTIVE NPO DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS across various customers and use cases, and expects some of that revenue to kick in IN 2028, with NPO starting to grow significantly from 2028. Critically, MACOM says it will NOT build or supply optical engines - in Data Center it is a chip supplier, not a multichip assembly or module supplier. It describes the architectural evolution as pluggable transceivers with DSPs, to LPO platforms that remove the DSP, morphing into smaller package-less NPO platforms; those architectures still need drivers and TIAs, but with much higher density - smaller parts, more channels, lower power, and varied form factors using wire bonds, bumped devices or flip chip, plus through-silicon-via options. Because these solutions are specific to the architectures hyperscalers are driving, the design wins come directly to MACOM. Related applications include LPO and LRO on single mode or multimode.

CEO Steve Daly called bringing a CW laser into production in 2028 'a watershed moment' that could be a very large revenue contributor. Separately, demand for MACOM's 25G DFB lasers (100G QSFP, CWDM4, LR4) is rising with urgency because of a GENERAL SUPPLY SHORTAGE OF INDIUM PHOSPHIDE DFB LASERS. MACOM expects to gain meaningful indium phosphide market share over the next three years; its Ann Arbor, Michigan facility has built photodiodes for over a decade and grows its own epitaxy by MBE.

quarterly_data.signal: ADI's optical franchise targets the CONTROL PATH, not the electro-optic data path: 'there are two critical pathways, the data path of electro optics and the control path, which guides, optimizes, and ensures the integrity of the data path. Data center optical revenue grew MORE THAN 100% year-over-year in fiscal Q3 2026 (data center is now 80% of ADI communications revenue, which itself was +84% YoY).

quarterly_data.signal: POWER franchise detail: customers are pushing for greater than 98% conversion efficiency, multi-kilowatt delivery with peak power up to 2x rated load, plus protection, telemetry and fault recording. Significant design uptick for ADI protection and 800V-to-intermediate conversion technology delivering 20 kW at industry-leading power density exceeding 2.5 kW per cubic inch, as the industry transitions to 800V DC power distribution. At the intermediate-to-core conversion layer - called ONE OF THE FASTEST AND LARGEST GROWING ANALOG OPPORTUNITIES IN THE AI ERA - ADI combines advanced power conversion, intelligent system control and real-time telemetry for next-generation processors operating at 6,000 A and sub-1V. Framing on efficiency: a 97% converter loses roughly 50% more energy as heat than a 98% one, compounding into cooling infrastructure and opex.
quarterly_data.figure: 800V->intermediate: 20 kW at >2.5 kW/cubic inch; core rails 6,000 A at sub-1V; >98% efficiency

quarterly_data.signal: Empower Semiconductor acquisition CLOSED July 7, 2026 for $1.5 BILLION in an all-cash transaction, extending ADI's vertical power story by taking power INTO THE PROCESSOR PACKAGE itself. In large-scale AI deployments the architecture reduces compute power consumption and temperature by approximately 10%-15%, equating to roughly $30 MILLION IN ANNUAL SAVINGS IN A 1 GW DATA CENTER. Cash and short-term investments fell to $2.3B on the close; net leverage ratio now 0.9.
quarterly_data.figure: Empower closed 07-07-2026 for $1.5B cash; -10-15% compute power/temp; ~$30M/yr saved per 1GW DC

quarterly_data.signal: GRID-TO-CHIP strategy: data center capacity is now measured in GIGAWATTS rather than FLOPS/TOPS and POWER AVAILABILITY HAS BECOME THE PRIMARY CONSTRAINT TO FURTHER AI PROGRESS. ADI supplies grid monitoring (real-time voltage, current, power quality, system health) to utilities, energy operators and infrastructure providers, plus battery management for energy storage - one of the grid's fastest-growing sectors. To accelerate time-to-power, hyperscalers are increasingly exploring DEDICATED MICROGRIDS, opening additional growth avenues that augment ADI's $500M+ energy business (inflected in 2025, accelerating in 2026). ADI now spans the entire electricity value chain: generation, transmission, storage, distribution, rack power and ultimately processor power delivery - 'essentially the vascular system of the data center.'

quarterly_data.signal: 2030 SAM RESET: ADI's current assessment is that its 2030 data center AND energy SAM has MORE THAN DOUBLED versus what it envisioned just one year ago - driven not simply by higher AI infrastructure CapEx but by new markets and architectures requiring ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE MORE ANALOG CONTENT delivered via higher-value solutions. Supporting math from the call: ~100 GW equivalent of data center infrastructure is expected to be built between now and 2031, with EACH GIGAWATT generating a $1B-$1.5B analog SAM. Runway seen extending to at least 2030 for strong double-digit data center growth; the ~$0.5B energy business is expected to DOUBLE by the end of the decade. ADI is contemplating long-term company growth above the 5%-7% model set at its 2021 investor day.

It takes about four years to make a craftsman and a journeyman, and he sees no oversupply of craft-skilled labour in the near future. quarterly_data.signal: VERTICAL INTEGRATION INTO CRITICAL-PATH EQUIPMENT. Duke Austin, asked where else he would add manufacturing after transformers and a utility pole company: 'We did the breaker deal with HICO. I thought that was a critical path for us and the high-voltage breakers are very difficult to get. You've seen us build them and partner.' The rule he states: 'Anywhere there's a critical path that we think we can invest capital to move it forward, that's what you've seen us do... we're taking advantage of areas where there's underinvestment', and those vertical supply-chain investments are 'showing up in synergies'. He will stay selective - EBOS companies are explicitly not a focus. The other leg is integrated fabrication: about seven million square feet of fabrication space, plus roughly 0.5 million square feet added with the recent acquisitions, with VDC (virtual design and construction) engineering in front of it so modules are designed for constructability. Done collaboratively with the client it takes total installed cost down significantly and de-risks logistics; the Phalcon acquisition puts that capacity in the Northeast, close to where the work is.

Quanta sells direct to the hyperscalers and to the larger technology customers, and can self-perform 'call it 80% of what a data center build is, maybe 90%', taking balance-of-plant scope and full-scale data-center opportunities on more and more sites; it is also picking up work at semiconductor plants, at manufacturing and medical facilities, and at Tesla. The pitch is speed and certainty: 'Technology is trying to move as fast as possible. Utilities are working to protect the ratepayer, and Quanta sits in the middle of that nexus.' On state-level data-center moratoriums (New York): immaterial - 'nothing really gets built there' - and these are eight- to ten-year developments, not one-year builds, with multiyear projects extending well beyond 2030.

quarterly_data.signal: WHERE THE BOTTLENECK ACTUALLY IS: interconnection and utility-scale generation, not Quanta's labour. Duke Austin: 'I'm not sure people understand that nexus and how difficult it is to interconnect to the grid and how much we're right in the middle of that interconnection', pointing at 'the queues on the utility side of substations, all the substations that are out there. We're right in the middle of that.' 'It takes generation and substations to get to the queue', and many data centers want to connect back to the grid at some point, which utilities do better than anyone. On generation he says it is 'technically difficult to have capacity to build combined cycles at the levels and speed desired', and that orders for engines placed today often carry a five- to six-year lead time - which he reads as evidence of how long this build lasts. Quanta does EPC on generation both in front of the meter and behind the meter, small engines through big engines, but will not take the risk on the combined-cycle side and some single-cycle engines without the contract terms it needs; some utilities are attempting to self-perform gas generation RFPs because of inadequate resources, which he has seen fail before.

quarterly_data.signal: FOUNDING INVESTOR IN HELIX DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE alongside KKR (lead), NVIDIA and the Kuwait Investment Authority — a platform combining power solutions for data centers with land and other digital infrastructure to create a 'RACK-TO-GRID one-stop shop' that customers increasingly prefer. Vistra's role is twofold: (1) commit UP TO $1B over time, with any amount above $500M subject to achieving certain milestones; (2) serve as the PREFERRED POWER PARTNER, participating in Helix development projects via contracted new-build or new contracts on existing assets. KKR approached Vistra for the preferred-power-partner role. Vistra retains optionality to develop projects on its own; where it does not supply the power it is 'effectively carried' in its financial investment. Helix launched in June 2026, is being staffed for development by KKR, expects to add more investors over time, and is in direct conversations with all of the major hyperscalers.

quarterly_data.signal: Helix is designed to absorb the capital Vistra does not want on its own balance sheet: 'if it's required to do things like POWERED SHELLS, POWERED LAND, that's something we don't believe our shareholders are expecting us to put a lot of capital in.' It also simplifies what are today multi-party negotiations on Vistra's existing sites (hyperscaler + co-location developer + equipment providers). quarterly_data.signal: LOAD-GROWTH VIEW UPDATED: annual load growth of at least 4-6% in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM through 2030 remain reasonable estimates (Q1 2026 framing was 'at least 5-6%' for ERCOT). NEW ALL-TIME SUMMER PEAKS set in July 2026 — PJM over 168 GW and ERCOT over 91 GW — and the grids met them, which Vistra argues disproves the claim that these markets cannot handle the load growth. Data centers matter 'particularly in 2028 and beyond', but a significant part of the growth is industrial reshoring, electrification, Texas population growth and broader economic expansion: of the ~5-6% ERCOT CAGR, ~3% is non-data-center (oil & gas, residential, small business) and ~2% is data centers.

quarterly_data.signal: ERCOT QUEUE REALITY CHECK: Vistra's May-2024 forecast of 115-120 GW of ERCOT load in 2030 is UNCHANGED despite the queue growing to what has at times been expressed as OVER 400 GW — Vistra thinks the real data-center number is 12-15 GW by 2030, i.e. the queue overstates demand by MORE THAN 20x. Governor Abbott's directive triggers a data-center audit that will likely pause ERCOT/PUC reviews for 'a couple of months'; Batch Zero baseload results were expected imminently and will slip. Vistra supports thinning the queue. Its Comanche Peak project targets energization at END OF 2027 and is not seen as affected; Vistra has projects in Batch Zero baseload, Batch Zero to-be-studied load and the coming Batch One. Only near-term energizations are at delay risk.
quarterly_data.figure: ERCOT 2030 load 115-120 GW (unchanged); queue >400 GW vs real DC 12-15 GW = >20x overstated

quarterly_data.signal: NEW-BUILD ECONOMICS GAP: ERCOT year-to-date wholesale power has averaged $30/MWh (same as last year) versus the ~$90/MWh area cited for new-build contracting — '30 is not going to get new stuff built.' The price of generation EQUIPMENT 'has doubled, if not tripled' in some cases, so what was an acceptable build price a year or two ago no longer is. In PJM the $555/MW-day RPB cap 'might get some things built' but a spread around it will be needed for certain projects. Large-load customers are willing to contract with EXISTING assets at a PREMIUM because it is still a discount to new build; co-location can beat even an islanded new build on speed.

quarterly_data.signal: ERCOT SCARCITY-PRICING MECHANICS (Head of Commercial): on July 22, 2026 a ~3.5-hour window as solar dropped off required ~25 GWh of battery discharge against only ~31 GWh available on the system, yet the day cleared just $57/MWh because batteries, knowing they would not run out, chased the bottom to deplete energy — 'very easy that that day could have cleared closer to a $400 or $500 day.' Battery returns since the large post-August-2023 ECRS payments have been about ONE FIFTH of investor expectations and battery queues are slowing. Vistra reads current ERCOT softness as recency bias plus lumpy load timing; the load it expects to hook up was always a 2027-2028 event.

quarterly_data.signal: REGULATORY: FERC's JUNE 2026 CO-LOCATION ORDER directs PJM and its transmission owners to accommodate co-location and adopt the corresponding transmission services — 'the order itself adopted a lot of Vistra's arguments.' The large-load contracting framework has four pillars: long-term contracts (the OpenAI contract is 25 years), minimum bills covering at least 100% of the incremental cost to serve, default/termination provisions, and default payments tied to collateral. Poroch said forms of collateral include parent guarantees, lines of credit and surety bonds depending on counterparty credit quality, with the aim of a collateral portfolio equivalent to about A- or better. He initially cited '$20.8 billion of collateral... in the aggregate on full ramp' and then clarified that this refers to the entire portfolio: 'the whole portfolio of the 17 GW, we got about $21 billion of collateral.' Minimum bills effectively decouple revenue from actual customer ramp rates, which Womack said often differ from what was predicted at project approval.

edges.relationship: fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) for AMD AI chips

contracts.signal: Chairman: PTI has become a supply-chain partner for AMD AI chips and will provide AMD fan-out PLP (panel-level packaging) solutions, and is actively pursuing additional AMD AI-chip applications. Despite equipment-delivery delays and parallel qualification, the AMD program is on schedule; PTI is confident of volume production before the middle of next year at the converted former-AUO fab, where the G7 panel equipment supporting AMD is installed and in qualification - which would make PTI the first company globally to mass-produce fan-out PLP for AI applications.

edges.relationship: joint venture (Singapore) for fine-line RDL-on-substrate fan-out packaging, serving Broadcom exclusively

contracts.signal: PTI and Broadcom will form a joint venture in Singapore - a major milestone making PTI a strategic and preferred partner of Broadcom. Built on PTI's fan-out PLP AI packaging experience, the JV will co-develop and produce additive-process fine-line-width redistribution-layer (RDL) packaging directly on advanced substrates (fan-out based), and will serve Broadcom exclusively without affecting PTI's fan-out PLP work for existing and future customers. An NDA is signed and the deal awaits Taiwan investment-authority approval, after which details will be disclosed; the JV funding goes in staged installments and does not raise PTI's NT$500 hundred million capex. The cooperation also brought PTI into the optical-communications field (Optical Engine, CPO switch roadmap).
